paper.title: Practical and Optimal Algorithm for Linear Contextual Bandits with Rare Parameter Updates

settings.name_in_paper: Linear Contextual Bandits with Batched Feedback (rare parameter updates)
unmapped: K-arm feature sets A_t drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution D, with arbitrary correlation within a round
rewards revealed only at the end of each interval of a static grid; reward-free within-interval context adaptivity allowed; O(log log T) parameter updates
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t \in [T]$, the agent observes contextual features of $K$ arms $\mathcal{A}_t := \{x_{t,1}, \dots, x_{t,K}\} \subseteq \RR^d$ and selects one arm $x_{t,a_t} \in \mathcal{A}_t$, receiving the reward $r_t = \langle x_{t,a_t}, \theta^* \rangle + \eta_t$ ... we assume that each feature set $\mathcal{A}_t$ is drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution $\mathcal{D}$ across rounds

settings.name_in_paper: Generalized Linear Contextual Bandits with Batched Feedback
unmapped: K-arm feature sets drawn i.i.d. from unknown distribution D
rewards revealed only at interval ends of a static grid (O(log log T) parameter updates)
rewards almost surely supported on [0,R] with R known (self-concordance |mu''| <= R mu')
settings.definition_quote: We next consider generalized linear contextual bandits, where rewards follow a one-parameter exponential family distribution... Following \citet{sawarni2024generalized}, we assume i.i.d. contexts drawn from an unknown distribution $\mathcal D$ and rewards almost surely supported on $[0,R]$ for a known constant $R>0$.

conditions: context sets i.i.d. from unknown distribution D
tuning: static schedule with O(log log T) parameter updates

source.label: thm:BLCE_g
source.quote: Suppose that Assumptions~\ref{assum:norm} and \ref{assum:subgauss} hold and that the context sets $\{\mathcal{A}_t\}_{t=1}^T$ are drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution $\mathcal{D}$. Run \texttt{BLCE-G} for $T$ rounds, using $\lambda = \log (dT)$, and any fixed constant $c\in(0,1)$. The worst-case cumulative regret satisfies \mathcal{R}(T) = \Ocal(\sqrt{dT}(\sqrt{\log(KT)} \wedge \sqrt{d+\log T})\sqrt{\log d\log\log T}) = \tilde{\Ocal}(\sqrt{dT\log K} \wedge d\sqrt{T}).

results.notes: Regret defined via expected inner products, so pseudo-regret. Also restated as O_tilde(sqrt(dT log K) ∧ d sqrt T). Proof uses d >= 3 and T >= d. Runtime O(K d^2 T (d + log log T)).

conditions: context sets i.i.d. from unknown distribution D (relaxable to batch-wise conditions of Remark 1)
tuning: static schedule with O(log log T) parameter updates

source.label: thm:BLCE
source.quote: Suppose that Assumptions~\ref{assum:norm} and \ref{assum:subgauss} hold and that the context sets $\{A_t\}_{t=1}^T$ are drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution $\mathcal{D}$. Run \texttt{BLCE} for $T$ rounds, using $\lambda = 1$, and any fixed constant $c\in(0,1)$. The worst-case cumulative regret satisfies \mathcal{R}(T) = \Ocal(\sqrt{dT}(\sqrt{\log(KT)} \wedge \sqrt{d+\log T})\sqrt{\log T\log\log T}) = \tilde{\Ocal}(\sqrt{dT\log K} \wedge d\sqrt{T}).

results.notes: No G-optimal design; runtime O(K d^2 T log log T). Remark 1 states the bound holds under weaker batch-wise conditional-independence assumptions on contexts.

bound.expression_latex: \Ocal(RS\sqrt{d(d+\log T)T\log T\log\log T / \hat\kappa}) + \Ocal((R^2Se^{8RS}d(d+\log T)\log T\log\log T + \frac{R}{\log\log T})T^{1/3})

symbols.R_r: known upper bound of the reward support [0,R]
symbols.kappa_hat: 1 / E_{A~D}[mu'(<x*,theta*>)], reciprocal of average curvature at the optimal arm

conditions: log-partition m convex and three times differentiable
MLE satisfies ||theta_hat||_2 <= S (or projected estimator used)

source.label: thm:bgle
source.quote: Suppose that Assumptions~\ref{assum:GLM_norm} and \ref{assum:GLM_diff} ... hold, that the context sets are drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution $\mathcal{D}$, and that rewards are almost surely supported on $[0,R]$. ... Run \texttt{BGLE} for $T$ rounds, using the known bounds $R$ and $S$, $\lambda=R^2(d+\log T)$, and any fixed constant $c\in(0,1)$ ... \mathcal{R}(T) = \Ocal(RS\sqrt{d(d+\log T)T\log T\log\log T / \hat\kappa}) + \Ocal((R^2Se^{8RS}d(d+\log T)\log T\log\log T + \frac{R}{\log\log T})T^{1/3}) = \widetilde{\Ocal}(RSd\sqrt{T}/\sqrt{\hat\kappa})+\widetilde\Ocal((R^{2}Se^{8RS}d^2+R)T^{1/3}).

results.notes: Instance-dependent through kappa_hat. Regret defined via expected mean-reward differences (pseudo-regret). Compute requires MLE oracle at interval boundaries.
